purpose: Fresh, broad sustainability audit of representative public visitor tasks using current live evidence and explicitly selected owner-supplied source

protocol.states: Initial desktop, then same document resized to 360 CSS px, live reduced-motion and dark changes, print emulation, twelve Tab presses; separate fresh no-JavaScript and dark contexts. Resized and emulated states are not independent cold loads or real-device tests.
protocol.measurementPurpose: Qualitative review and bounded interaction evidence, not headline bytes or energy
limitations: Main document observations; embedded frames are not traversed
Page probes include bounded Tab traversal after other states; no control activation. Journey actions must be explicit
Selected CDP response headers omit cookies and authorization; no header alone proves cache reuse
Keyboard trace is twelve Tab presses, not complete keyboard or accessibility conformance
Resource Timing zeros may reflect timing restrictions or cache, not zero traffic
Notification requestPermission calls counted with a delegating wrapper
Print emulation is not PDF pagination or document accessibility testing

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess visible distractions against the declared visitor task; distinguish useful prompts from interruptions.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Inspect choice wording, defaults, prominence and the observed accept/reject paths for undue steering. DOM text alone does not establish visual parity.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess the sampled task's wording, headings and terminology for its stated audience; retain uncertainty about unrepresented users.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Compare repeated navigation and control names across sampled pages; consistent samples do not prove a documented design system.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess observed animation purpose, playback controls and reduced-motion behavior. A quiet snapshot does not prove no motion occurs elsewhere.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Assess observed alerts and notification permission requests for user value and choice; absence is limited to observed states.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Review print layout visibility and download labels for the declared task. Fetch and inspect document content before asserting optimization or equivalence.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Use initial JS/CSS execution observations to nominate investigation targets; require representative journeys or source corroboration before recommending removal.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Relate initial script resources to visible components and later task needs; recommend splitting only when a component's deferred use and usable activation are corroborated.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Compare narrow and desktop task content and overflow, then exercise affected controls; width emulation alone is not real-device compatibility.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Identify consequential user choices in the sample and assess whether contextual impact information is useful and supported. Do not prescribe carbon labels on every control.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Execute declared task actions and inspect completion evidence; an expected selector is one observable, not proof of user success or optimal journey length.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Cite page/state or journey JSON Pointers, declared task and sample. Use additional screenshots, task observations, document content or source when the expectation cannot be resolved from the collected facts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled task images preserve useful content and provide proportionate intrinsic dimensions and delivery choices for their rendered size and pixel density. A large image is an investigation candidate until legibility and task value are checked; absent srcset alone is not a failure.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Compare desktop/narrow image dimensions, srcset/sizes, delivered MIME types, loading state, and task content. Confirm any proposed rendition at intended pixel densities before asserting savings.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Observed web fonts and variants serve the sampled content, with a declared fallback/loading strategy where needed. Do not fail a site merely for using a web font; recommend removal or subsetting only after language and readability requirements are established.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect document.fonts family/weight/style/display/status, font responses and visible body text. Missing font-blocking/constrained-loading or language evidence can leave the scoped judgment unresolved.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled document has a meaningful language, primary heading and main region, and task controls have visible labels or an explicit naming relationship. Count/attribute presence alone does not establish semantic correctness or WCAG compliance.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Read title/lang/headings/mainCount, form control labels and task content. aria-labelledby references need resolution before claiming a missing accessible name.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled content has a descriptive title and usable canonical metadata when applicable; declared structured-data blocks parse as JSON. Judge description and other optional metadata according to page purpose, not a mandatory-field checklist.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect metadata and document title, resolving canonical URLs and applicability. JSON parsing does not establish schema validity or search-engine eligibility.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled page respects applicable dark/reduced-motion preferences both before navigation and when they change in-page, without losing task content. Distinguish intentional design choices and absence of applicable motion from unsupported behavior.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Compare desktop, reduced_motion, live_dark and cold_dark observations, colors, visible text and actual animations. A matching media query alone is insufficient; theme initialization and live change are distinct.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled core reading content and navigation remain available without JavaScript, or an explicit alternative supports the task. This bounded check does not establish no-JavaScript search, every interaction, or all browser compatibility.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Compare desktop and fresh no_javascript text/headings/navigation. Explain task-critical missing content and legitimate progressive enhancements rather than demanding every feature without scripts.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Repeated observed API requests are justified by the sampled task and its update needs. Identify redundant-looking requests for investigation without inferring backend cost or safe removal from URL repetition alone.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect bounded network.requests methods/types/timestamps and explicit journey resource entries. Establish polling purpose, cache behavior and task freshness needs; initial-only windows may remain cantTell.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Reusable public scripts/styles/media expose an appropriate caching or validation policy in the sample. Distinguish dynamic/private responses and note that headers alone do not prove cache reuse or offline support.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Review allowlisted response cache-control/etag/last-modified/age/vary headers and public resource purpose. Require a warm-load test before claiming measured reuse; private no-store is a legitimate exception.

checkDefinitions.expectation: Material sampled text assets are delivered with compression where beneficial. Do not demand compression for already-compressed images, tiny bodies or error responses without context.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Review text/script/style response MIME types, status and content-encoding, alongside transfer magnitude when available. Header absence for a material text response supports investigation; missing response evidence stays unknown.

checkDefinitions.expectation: The sampled initial keyboard path reaches visible task navigation/controls in a meaningful order with a discernible focus indicator. A bounded Tab trace cannot establish complete keyboard support, reverse navigation, traps or screen-reader accessibility.
checkDefinitions.evidenceRequirements: Inspect keyboardFocus steps, names/label relationships, element geometry, focus-visible and outline clues. A zero outline is not proof of invisible focus because borders or shadows may supply it; verify the actual indicator before a failure.

Do your best work

Wagtail is a CMS that supports everyone’s creativity

Whether you're a developer who wants the freedom to build a custom feature or an editor who wants to focus more on content than code, Wagtail encourages the ingenuity of each member of a content team.

See how real orgs use Wagtail

Join us for Wagtail Space 2026, a FREE and flexible online event

StreamField
Make content the way you want to

With Wagtail StreamField, Editors have the freedom to build pages the way they want to without coding. Developers love it too because StreamField gives them precise control over how content is displayed and how data is organized.

Intuitive content organization

Find and organize content easily

The intuitive Wagtail administration panel makes it easy to find and organize your content whether you have a handful of blog posts or thousands of pages to organize. With the Wagtail sidebar, you have a quick options to find content you need.

Customizable page types

Create and extend custom content types

Wagtail page types make it easy for developers to create and extend a custom architecture. Whether your team needs a blog post or a case study or a donation page, you can spin it up quickly without a ton of database wrangling.

Snippets

Create reusable components

With Wagtail Snippets, there’s no need to waste time recreating components that you use on multiple different pages. Snippets offer developers a quick way to add reusable components to the Wagtail administrative panel so editors can use them over and over again where they want to.

Form builder

Create contact forms, surveys, and more

Empower your content creators to interact with readers using the Wagtail custom form builder. After some simple configuration on the backend, editors can use Wagtail forms to create contact forms, surveys, and more.

Advanced image management
Keep your image library organised and under control

With the image focal point and custom cropping tools in Wagtail, you have more control over how images are cropped and displayed. The multiple image upload and image deduplication features also help you keep your image library organized and under control.

Give Wagtail a go
Try the starter kit

See if Wagtail is right for you

You can deploy a working Wagtail site in as little as 15 minutes.

Build your first site

Our 10 min install guide

Follow our tutorial to build a brand new Wagtail project.

Frontend freedom

Integrate with the frontend technology of your choice

With the Wagtail templating system, your designers and frontend developers have complete frontend freedom. Wagtail can be integrated with the frontend technology of your choice, and you can even choose to operate Wagtail as a headless CMS with multiple frontends.

Explore some of our Wagtail success stories
Turning five hospital websites into one

With Wagtail, Children's Health Ireland took 5 disjointed websites and merge them into one website with smoother, more efficient workflows.

How we came to love Wagtail at Berkeley

When developers at University of California, Berkeley went looking for a Drupal replacement, they found Wagtail and fell in love with it. Here's why.

Read more success stories

See how governments, charities, cultural institutions, and private businesses are using Wagtail.

Open, extensible, and dependable

The code for Wagtail is completely open source.

Wagtail is powered by Python and Django, two of the most popular and powerful open source technologies available. The code for Wagtail is completely open source and supported by an active community and core contributors from agencies around the world. The founding creators, Torchbox, are an employee-owned trust dedicated to serving nonprofits and public organisations rather than investors. The source code is free and open so anyone can customise and extend Wagtail.

Build accessible experiences with Wagtail

A CMS that centers accessibility

The Wagtail administration panel targets WCAG 2.2 AA and all ATAG 2.0 checkpoints, making it accessible for editors with disabilities, not just visitors. Built-in accessibility checkers, alt text prompts, and heading validation will also help your team create compliant content from day one.

See Wagtail's accessibility statement

Accessibility checker

Catch accessibility issues before you publish

The built-in Wagtail accessibility checker flags likely accessibility issues in content. The checker is customizable so you can go beyond the default rules and set up standards specific to your code and your organization.

Alt text tools

Encourage better alt text practices

Wagtail supports contextual alt text and marking images as decorative to provide better experiences for screen reader users. The accessibility checker also flags common alt text issues like using file names in alt text.

Dark mode and high contrast

Customize your themes and contrast

Wagtail provides dark mode and a high contrast theme options for users who live with light sensitivity, eye strain, and other visual conditions. Dark mode also uses less energy on OLED screens, which makes it a plus for the planet too.

Keyboard navigation

Shortcuts and commands for keyboard lovers

If you love or need your keyboard to get around, Wagtail includes keyboard commands and shortcuts to help you get where you need to go. The Wagtail slash command quickly opens block menus and formatting options, so you can quickly build your content without clicking around.

Power up your content with optional AI features

Use the official Wagtail AI package to add your favorite AI tools

Whether you prefer GPT or Claude or one of the growing number of LLM open source models, Wagtail AI gives you the option to use AI to enhance your content. Save time on creating image labels, titles, summaries, and more. Get automatic page suggestions or receive feedback on your content. Wagtail AI suggests content — never mandates it, so creators have full control.

Check out Wagtail AI

Advanced enterprise workflows

Designed to support content teams

Wagtail comes with features that support the whole publishing process from writing the first draft to copyediting to publication. Wagtail supports each step you need to create flawless content, no matter how many steps you need.

Site history

Full transparency into who has made changes

With the site history feature, you’ll have full transparency into who has made changes to your content and how. You can log and audit user actions with the site history report directly in the Wagtail administrative panel or through a backend management command.

Customisable workflows

Control who can moderate, review, and publish content

Whether you need one editing step or many, the custom workflows in Wagtail give you options to add as little or as much content review as you need. The fine permissions in Wagtail make it easy to control who can moderate, review, and publish content.

Revision rollbacks

Rollback to the version that you want to share with the world

Editing often involves multiple revisions and it can be hard to keep track of the changes made from version to version. Wagtail includes a built-in revision comparison tool that can help you rollback to the version that you want to share with the world.

Scheduling

Take full control over your editorial calendar

You can schedule posts to go live whenever you choose and you can set an expiration date on content so that your time-limited posts are automatically unpublished.

Commenting and notifications
Editors can review and request content changes directly in Wagtail

With the Wagtail commenting feature, you don’t need to fuss with collecting comments in another text editor. Email notifications also make it easy for you to know when new comments are made or a piece of content moves to the next step in your publishing process.

Wagtail Space 2026

18-20 November

Find out more

Enter a search term
Do your best work

Wagtail is a CMS that supports everyone’s creativity

Whether you're a developer who wants the freedom to build a custom feature or an editor who wants to focus more on content than code, Wagtail encourages the ingenuity of each member of a content team.

See how real orgs use Wagtail

Join us for Wagtail Space 2026, a FREE and flexible online event

StreamField
Make content the way you want to

With Wagtail StreamField, Editors have the freedom to build pages the way they want to without coding. Developers love it too because StreamField gives them precise control over how content is displayed and how data is organized.

Intuitive content organization

Find and organize content easily

The intuitive Wagtail administration panel makes it easy to find and organize your content whether you have a handful of blog posts or thousands of pages to organize. With the Wagtail sidebar, you have a quick options to find content you need.

Customizable page types

Create and extend custom content types

Wagtail page types make it easy for developers to create and extend a custom architecture. Whether your team needs a blog post or a case study or a donation page, you can spin it up quickly without a ton of database wrangling.

Snippets

Create reusable components

With Wagtail Snippets, there’s no need to waste time recreating components that you use on multiple different pages. Snippets offer developers a quick way to add reusable components to the Wagtail administrative panel so editors can use them over and over again where they want to.

Form builder

Create contact forms, surveys, and more

Empower your content creators to interact with readers using the Wagtail custom form builder. After some simple configuration on the backend, editors can use Wagtail forms to create contact forms, surveys, and more.

Advanced image management
Keep your image library organised and under control

With the image focal point and custom cropping tools in Wagtail, you have more control over how images are cropped and displayed. The multiple image upload and image deduplication features also help you keep your image library organized and under control.

Give Wagtail a go
Try the starter kit

See if Wagtail is right for you

You can deploy a working Wagtail site in as little as 15 minutes.

Build your first site

Our 10 min install guide

Follow our tutorial to build a brand new Wagtail project.

Frontend freedom

Integrate with the frontend technology of your choice

With the Wagtail templating system, your designers and frontend developers have complete frontend freedom. Wagtail can be integrated with the frontend technology of your choice, and you can even choose to operate Wagtail as a headless CMS with multiple frontends.

Explore some of our Wagtail success stories
Turning five hospital websites into one

With Wagtail, Children's Health Ireland took 5 disjointed websites and merge them into one website with smoother, more efficient workflows.

How we came to love Wagtail at Berkeley

When developers at University of California, Berkeley went looking for a Drupal replacement, they found Wagtail and fell in love with it. Here's why.

Read more success stories

See how governments, charities, cultural institutions, and private businesses are using Wagtail.

Open, extensible, and dependable

The code for Wagtail is completely open source.

Wagtail is powered by Python and Django, two of the most popular and powerful open source technologies available. The code for Wagtail is completely open source and supported by an active community and core contributors from agencies around the world. The founding creators, Torchbox, are an employee-owned trust dedicated to serving nonprofits and public organisations rather than investors. The source code is free and open so anyone can customise and extend Wagtail.

Build accessible experiences with Wagtail

A CMS that centers accessibility

The Wagtail administration panel targets WCAG 2.2 AA and all ATAG 2.0 checkpoints, making it accessible for editors with disabilities, not just visitors. Built-in accessibility checkers, alt text prompts, and heading validation will also help your team create compliant content from day one.

See Wagtail's accessibility statement

Accessibility checker

Catch accessibility issues before you publish

The built-in Wagtail accessibility checker flags likely accessibility issues in content. The checker is customizable so you can go beyond the default rules and set up standards specific to your code and your organization.

Alt text tools

Encourage better alt text practices

Wagtail supports contextual alt text and marking images as decorative to provide better experiences for screen reader users. The accessibility checker also flags common alt text issues like using file names in alt text.

Dark mode and high contrast

Customize your themes and contrast

Wagtail provides dark mode and a high contrast theme options for users who live with light sensitivity, eye strain, and other visual conditions. Dark mode also uses less energy on OLED screens, which makes it a plus for the planet too.

Keyboard navigation

Shortcuts and commands for keyboard lovers

If you love or need your keyboard to get around, Wagtail includes keyboard commands and shortcuts to help you get where you need to go. The Wagtail slash command quickly opens block menus and formatting options, so you can quickly build your content without clicking around.

Power up your content with optional AI features

Use the official Wagtail AI package to add your favorite AI tools

Whether you prefer GPT or Claude or one of the growing number of LLM open source models, Wagtail AI gives you the option to use AI to enhance your content. Save time on creating image labels, titles, summaries, and more. Get automatic page suggestions or receive feedback on your content. Wagtail AI suggests content — never mandates it, so creators have full control.

Check out Wagtail AI

Advanced enterprise workflows

Designed to support content teams

Wagtail comes with features that support the whole publishing process from writing the first draft to copyediting to publication. Wagtail supports each step you need to create flawless content, no matter how many steps you need.

Site history

Full transparency into who has made changes

With the site history feature, you’ll have full transparency into who has made changes to your content and how. You can log and audit user actions with the site history report directly in the Wagtail administrative panel or through a backend management command.

Customisable workflows

Control who can moderate, review, and publish content

Whether you need one editing step or many, the custom workflows in Wagtail give you options to add as little or as much content review as you need. The fine permissions in Wagtail make it easy to control who can moderate, review, and publish content.

Revision rollbacks

Rollback to the version that you want to share with the world

Editing often involves multiple revisions and it can be hard to keep track of the changes made from version to version. Wagtail includes a built-in revision comparison tool that can help you rollback to the version that you want to share with the world.

Scheduling

Take full control over your editorial calendar

You can schedule posts to go live whenever you choose and you can set an expiration date on content so that your time-limited posts are automatically unpublished.

Commenting and notifications
Editors can review and request content changes directly in Wagtail

With the Wagtail commenting feature, you don’t need to fuss with collecting comments in another text editor. Email notifications also make it easy for you to know when new comments are made or a piece of content moves to the next step in your publishing process.

See every single feature Wagtail has from live preview to multi-site.

Do your best work

Wagtail is a CMS that supports everyone’s creativity

Whether you're a developer who wants the freedom to build a custom feature or an editor who wants to focus more on content than code, Wagtail encourages the ingenuity of each member of a content team.

See how real orgs use Wagtail

Join us for Wagtail Space 2026, a FREE and flexible online event

StreamField
Make content the way you want to

With Wagtail StreamField, Editors have the freedom to build pages the way they want to without coding. Developers love it too because StreamField gives them precise control over how content is displayed and how data is organized.

Intuitive content organization

Find and organize content easily

The intuitive Wagtail administration panel makes it easy to find and organize your content whether you have a handful of blog posts or thousands of pages to organize. With the Wagtail sidebar, you have a quick options to find content you need.

Customizable page types

Create and extend custom content types

Wagtail page types make it easy for developers to create and extend a custom architecture. Whether your team needs a blog post or a case study or a donation page, you can spin it up quickly without a ton of database wrangling.

Snippets

Create reusable components

With Wagtail Snippets, there’s no need to waste time recreating components that you use on multiple different pages. Snippets offer developers a quick way to add reusable components to the Wagtail administrative panel so editors can use them over and over again where they want to.

Form builder

Create contact forms, surveys, and more

Empower your content creators to interact with readers using the Wagtail custom form builder. After some simple configuration on the backend, editors can use Wagtail forms to create contact forms, surveys, and more.

Advanced image management
Keep your image library organised and under control

With the image focal point and custom cropping tools in Wagtail, you have more control over how images are cropped and displayed. The multiple image upload and image deduplication features also help you keep your image library organized and under control.

Give Wagtail a go
Try the starter kit

See if Wagtail is right for you

You can deploy a working Wagtail site in as little as 15 minutes.

Build your first site

Our 10 min install guide

Follow our tutorial to build a brand new Wagtail project.

Frontend freedom

Integrate with the frontend technology of your choice

With the Wagtail templating system, your designers and frontend developers have complete frontend freedom. Wagtail can be integrated with the frontend technology of your choice, and you can even choose to operate Wagtail as a headless CMS with multiple frontends.

Explore some of our Wagtail success stories
Turning five hospital websites into one

With Wagtail, Children's Health Ireland took 5 disjointed websites and merge them into one website with smoother, more efficient workflows.

How we came to love Wagtail at Berkeley

When developers at University of California, Berkeley went looking for a Drupal replacement, they found Wagtail and fell in love with it. Here's why.

Read more success stories

See how governments, charities, cultural institutions, and private businesses are using Wagtail.

Open, extensible, and dependable

The code for Wagtail is completely open source.

Wagtail is powered by Python and Django, two of the most popular and powerful open source technologies available. The code for Wagtail is completely open source and supported by an active community and core contributors from agencies around the world. The founding creators, Torchbox, are an employee-owned trust dedicated to serving nonprofits and public organisations rather than investors. The source code is free and open so anyone can customise and extend Wagtail.

Build accessible experiences with Wagtail

A CMS that centers accessibility

The Wagtail administration panel targets WCAG 2.2 AA and all ATAG 2.0 checkpoints, making it accessible for editors with disabilities, not just visitors. Built-in accessibility checkers, alt text prompts, and heading validation will also help your team create compliant content from day one.

See Wagtail's accessibility statement

Accessibility checker

Catch accessibility issues before you publish

The built-in Wagtail accessibility checker flags likely accessibility issues in content. The checker is customizable so you can go beyond the default rules and set up standards specific to your code and your organization.

Alt text tools

Encourage better alt text practices

Wagtail supports contextual alt text and marking images as decorative to provide better experiences for screen reader users. The accessibility checker also flags common alt text issues like using file names in alt text.

Dark mode and high contrast

Customize your themes and contrast

Wagtail provides dark mode and a high contrast theme options for users who live with light sensitivity, eye strain, and other visual conditions. Dark mode also uses less energy on OLED screens, which makes it a plus for the planet too.

Keyboard navigation

Shortcuts and commands for keyboard lovers

If you love or need your keyboard to get around, Wagtail includes keyboard commands and shortcuts to help you get where you need to go. The Wagtail slash command quickly opens block menus and formatting options, so you can quickly build your content without clicking around.

Power up your content with optional AI features

Use the official Wagtail AI package to add your favorite AI tools

Whether you prefer GPT or Claude or one of the growing number of LLM open source models, Wagtail AI gives you the option to use AI to enhance your content. Save time on creating image labels, titles, summaries, and more. Get automatic page suggestions or receive feedback on your content. Wagtail AI suggests content — never mandates it, so creators have full control.

Check out Wagtail AI

Advanced enterprise workflows

Designed to support content teams

Wagtail comes with features that support the whole publishing process from writing the first draft to copyediting to publication. Wagtail supports each step you need to create flawless content, no matter how many steps you need.

Site history

Full transparency into who has made changes

With the site history feature, you’ll have full transparency into who has made changes to your content and how. You can log and audit user actions with the site history report directly in the Wagtail administrative panel or through a backend management command.

Customisable workflows

Control who can moderate, review, and publish content

Whether you need one editing step or many, the custom workflows in Wagtail give you options to add as little or as much content review as you need. The fine permissions in Wagtail make it easy to control who can moderate, review, and publish content.

Revision rollbacks

Rollback to the version that you want to share with the world

Editing often involves multiple revisions and it can be hard to keep track of the changes made from version to version. Wagtail includes a built-in revision comparison tool that can help you rollback to the version that you want to share with the world.

Scheduling

Take full control over your editorial calendar

You can schedule posts to go live whenever you choose and you can set an expiration date on content so that your time-limited posts are automatically unpublished.

Commenting and notifications
Editors can review and request content changes directly in Wagtail

With the Wagtail commenting feature, you don’t need to fuss with collecting comments in another text editor. Email notifications also make it easy for you to know when new comments are made or a piece of content moves to the next step in your publishing process.

See every single feature Wagtail has from live preview to multi-site.

Do your best work

Wagtail is a CMS that supports everyone’s creativity

Whether you're a developer who wants the freedom to build a custom feature or an editor who wants to focus more on content than code, Wagtail encourages the ingenuity of each member of a content team.

See how real orgs use Wagtail

Join us for Wagtail Space 2026, a FREE and flexible online event

StreamField
Make content the way you want to

With Wagtail StreamField, Editors have the freedom to build pages the way they want to without coding. Developers love it too because StreamField gives them precise control over how content is displayed and how data is organized.

Intuitive content organization

Find and organize content easily

The intuitive Wagtail administration panel makes it easy to find and organize your content whether you have a handful of blog posts or thousands of pages to organize. With the Wagtail sidebar, you have a quick options to find content you need.

Customizable page types

Create and extend custom content types

Wagtail page types make it easy for developers to create and extend a custom architecture. Whether your team needs a blog post or a case study or a donation page, you can spin it up quickly without a ton of database wrangling.

Snippets

Create reusable components

With Wagtail Snippets, there’s no need to waste time recreating components that you use on multiple different pages. Snippets offer developers a quick way to add reusable components to the Wagtail administrative panel so editors can use them over and over again where they want to.

Form builder

Create contact forms, surveys, and more

Empower your content creators to interact with readers using the Wagtail custom form builder. After some simple configuration on the backend, editors can use Wagtail forms to create contact forms, surveys, and more.

Advanced image management
Keep your image library organised and under control

With the image focal point and custom cropping tools in Wagtail, you have more control over how images are cropped and displayed. The multiple image upload and image deduplication features also help you keep your image library organized and under control.

Give Wagtail a go
Try the starter kit

See if Wagtail is right for you

You can deploy a working Wagtail site in as little as 15 minutes.

Build your first site

Our 10 min install guide

Follow our tutorial to build a brand new Wagtail project.

Frontend freedom

Integrate with the frontend technology of your choice

With the Wagtail templating system, your designers and frontend developers have complete frontend freedom. Wagtail can be integrated with the frontend technology of your choice, and you can even choose to operate Wagtail as a headless CMS with multiple frontends.

Explore some of our Wagtail success stories
Turning five hospital websites into one

With Wagtail, Children's Health Ireland took 5 disjointed websites and merge them into one website with smoother, more efficient workflows.

How we came to love Wagtail at Berkeley

When developers at University of California, Berkeley went looking for a Drupal replacement, they found Wagtail and fell in love with it. Here's why.

Read more success stories

See how governments, charities, cultural institutions, and private businesses are using Wagtail.

Open, extensible, and dependable

The code for Wagtail is completely open source.

Wagtail is powered by Python and Django, two of the most popular and powerful open source technologies available. The code for Wagtail is completely open source and supported by an active community and core contributors from agencies around the world. The founding creators, Torchbox, are an employee-owned trust dedicated to serving nonprofits and public organisations rather than investors. The source code is free and open so anyone can customise and extend Wagtail.

Build accessible experiences with Wagtail

A CMS that centers accessibility

The Wagtail administration panel targets WCAG 2.2 AA and all ATAG 2.0 checkpoints, making it accessible for editors with disabilities, not just visitors. Built-in accessibility checkers, alt text prompts, and heading validation will also help your team create compliant content from day one.

See Wagtail's accessibility statement

Accessibility checker

Catch accessibility issues before you publish

The built-in Wagtail accessibility checker flags likely accessibility issues in content. The checker is customizable so you can go beyond the default rules and set up standards specific to your code and your organization.

Alt text tools

Encourage better alt text practices

Wagtail supports contextual alt text and marking images as decorative to provide better experiences for screen reader users. The accessibility checker also flags common alt text issues like using file names in alt text.

Dark mode and high contrast

Customize your themes and contrast

Wagtail provides dark mode and a high contrast theme options for users who live with light sensitivity, eye strain, and other visual conditions. Dark mode also uses less energy on OLED screens, which makes it a plus for the planet too.

Keyboard navigation

Shortcuts and commands for keyboard lovers

If you love or need your keyboard to get around, Wagtail includes keyboard commands and shortcuts to help you get where you need to go. The Wagtail slash command quickly opens block menus and formatting options, so you can quickly build your content without clicking around.

Power up your content with optional AI features

Use the official Wagtail AI package to add your favorite AI tools

Whether you prefer GPT or Claude or one of the growing number of LLM open source models, Wagtail AI gives you the option to use AI to enhance your content. Save time on creating image labels, titles, summaries, and more. Get automatic page suggestions or receive feedback on your content. Wagtail AI suggests content — never mandates it, so creators have full control.

Check out Wagtail AI

Advanced enterprise workflows

Designed to support content teams

Wagtail comes with features that support the whole publishing process from writing the first draft to copyediting to publication. Wagtail supports each step you need to create flawless content, no matter how many steps you need.

Site history

Full transparency into who has made changes

With the site history feature, you’ll have full transparency into who has made changes to your content and how. You can log and audit user actions with the site history report directly in the Wagtail administrative panel or through a backend management command.

Customisable workflows

Control who can moderate, review, and publish content

Whether you need one editing step or many, the custom workflows in Wagtail give you options to add as little or as much content review as you need. The fine permissions in Wagtail make it easy to control who can moderate, review, and publish content.

Revision rollbacks

Rollback to the version that you want to share with the world

Editing often involves multiple revisions and it can be hard to keep track of the changes made from version to version. Wagtail includes a built-in revision comparison tool that can help you rollback to the version that you want to share with the world.

Scheduling

Take full control over your editorial calendar

You can schedule posts to go live whenever you choose and you can set an expiration date on content so that your time-limited posts are automatically unpublished.

Commenting and notifications
Editors can review and request content changes directly in Wagtail

With the Wagtail commenting feature, you don’t need to fuss with collecting comments in another text editor. Email notifications also make it easy for you to know when new comments are made or a piece of content moves to the next step in your publishing process.

See every single feature Wagtail has from live preview to multi-site.

Customisable workflows

Control who can moderate, review, and publish content

Whether you need one editing step or many, the custom workflows in Wagtail give you options to add as little or as much content review as you need. The fine permissions in Wagtail make it easy to control who can moderate, review, and publish content.

Revision rollbacks

Rollback to the version that you want to share with the world

Editing often involves multiple revisions and it can be hard to keep track of the changes made from version to version. Wagtail includes a built-in revision comparison tool that can help you rollback to the version that you want to share with the world.

Scheduling

Take full control over your editorial calendar

You can schedule posts to go live whenever you choose and you can set an expiration date on content so that your time-limited posts are automatically unpublished.

Commenting and notifications
Editors can review and request content changes directly in Wagtail

With the Wagtail commenting feature, you don’t need to fuss with collecting comments in another text editor. Email notifications also make it easy for you to know when new comments are made or a piece of content moves to the next step in your publishing process.

Automate more with an improved API and agent-ready tools in Wagtail 8.1
See how Wagtail 8.1 can help you be ready for what's next
Meagen Voss

Wagtail community manager

Previous post
A Wagtail demo in your browser

We are living through a big shift in how online content is created and consumed. Change is both exciting and scary. It's leading many people to ask, "What's happening to the Internet?"

Answering that question and then creating an online future that works for most people is going to take a lot more people and organizing and effort than a single open source project can provide. The way we're doing our part is by committing to make a CMS that gives users options instead of mandates.

Wagtail 8.1 continues to build on some of the key goals in our product strategy to equip our users for a future in which more people are using AI tools to automate tasks, build their own software, and interact with online content. Our last big release introduced a new version of the Wagtail REST API. This release includes an updated version of that API along with other features and tools to provide you with the flexibility you need to adapt to new advances and challenges of the Internet.

Write and fetch more content with the updated API

The newest version of the API includes more writeable content types, all typed according to the site’s data model. You can retrieve more detailed schemas for StreamField blocks and other data through the API now, which will help you access and edit more of your Wagtail content. Here is an example, inspecting what blocks are available on a content page and their exact fields:

We improved the Markdown output as well so that you can add more styled text for links, line breaks, multi-paragraph quotes, and nested lists. We also corrected the ways certain references are handled through the API and optimized the OpenAPI schema so it will work better for larger projects.

We're continuing to call this API a preview as we build and add more features. If there is anything you think we should prioritize, we definitely want to hear your feedback.

Access workflows through the API

One of the bigger changes we've added to the API in this release is the ability to access Wagtail workflows through the API. Workflows are used to moderate and review content in Wagtail. Now you can submit pages or snippets for moderation, approve or reject moderation tasks, resume a workflow after changes were requested, cancel workflows, and read a workflow’s status and history through the API.

You can still do all these tasks through the Wagtail admin. But with the new API access, you have even more options to automate and track tasks related to your workflows. And like with all API features, this is all documented and typed to simplify integration into other systems:

Add more automation with official agent skills and the prototype CLI

When we surveyed our community about the sort of AI-related developer features you wanted to see for Wagtail, two popular requests were official skills for AI coding assistants and an official CLI for automating certain tasks. We have a new collection of official agent skills for developers to try out. We've also done some research on how different models perform with these skills and how energy efficient they are so you can make informed choices about which models you'd like to use for your projects.

The CLI we're offering right now is a prototype and may still have some rough edges. But if you're experimenting with AI automation, it's a good option for you to test out ways to connect AI agents to your Wagtail projects through the API. We haven't heard of anyone letting their OpenClaw agent run absolutely wild with their Wagtail content (yet), but this CLI gives you the option to do just that if you enjoy living dangerously. And if you’d to see what that looks like as a demo, here is an example of combining the API, CLI, and skills to do content operations with DeepSeek Harness and Mistral Large 4:

Enhance your SEO metadata with the new SEO checks

The checks section has a new feature to help you optimize your metadata and make it more SEO-friendly. The meta titles and descriptions will appear in the checks section along with a rating of the lengths for each of them. The ratings are informed by typical search engine display budgets and will help you make your meta data better for search engines and bots to collect. There is also an option for you to view and review other meta tags for your page directly in the Wagtail admin. And it’s also available on all live pages, within the userbar:

Thank you to Freedom of the Press Foundation who helped make this happen via a feature sponsorship!

Serve different page representations from the same URL

Wagtail now has the option for you to offer the same page in different formats so that your content can be accessed more easily by different technologies. You could add a JSON format that makes your content easier to use through APIs, or you could use Markdown to make your content more digestible by AI agents, with less page furniture to go through. For example, here is what a blog post would look like transformed to Markdown:

This is a generic capability for all kinds of content negotiations, so you can add other content formats based on your own customization needs.

Faster, better multilingual sitemaps

Having a good sitemap helps make your content easier to catalog and digest by search engine crawlers and other bots. Our improvements in this release will help you create a sitemap that includes translated pages and includes all of the pages from different locales when you're using internationalization. That can increase the discoverability of your multilingual content and make it more likely to turn up in search results.

Here’s an example of what this looks like in practice, with the correct alternate hreflang meta tags:

We also now document how to cache generated sitemaps, which will definitely help for large sites.

Getting ready for your upgrade

Most of the big changes happened in our last major release, but there are still a few things to be aware of as you upgrade. First of all, if you are using internationalization, be aware that all of your locales will be added to your sitemap. Second, we are no longer supporting Python 3.10, so please upgrade to a newer version if you haven't already (Python 3.15 is supported!). Third, be aware that we plan to deprecate the v2 API in our next major release (9.0). The v2 API is fully supported in this release with no changes, but deprecation warnings will start appearing in Wagtail 8.2.

There are a few other deprecated functions to watch out for. You can read all about them in our full release notes. Let us know what you think, and join us at Wagtail Space to discuss the new release!

We improved the Markdown output as well so that you can add more styled text for links, line breaks, multi-paragraph quotes, and nested lists. We also corrected the ways certain references are handled through the API and optimized the OpenAPI schema so it will work better for larger projects.

We're continuing to call this API a preview as we build and add more features. If there is anything you think we should prioritize, we definitely want to hear your feedback.

Access workflows through the API

One of the bigger changes we've added to the API in this release is the ability to access Wagtail workflows through the API. Workflows are used to moderate and review content in Wagtail. Now you can submit pages or snippets for moderation, approve or reject moderation tasks, resume a workflow after changes were requested, cancel workflows, and read a workflow’s status and history through the API.

You can still do all these tasks through the Wagtail admin. But with the new API access, you have even more options to automate and track tasks related to your workflows. And like with all API features, this is all documented and typed to simplify integration into other systems:

Add more automation with official agent skills and the prototype CLI

When we surveyed our community about the sort of AI-related developer features you wanted to see for Wagtail, two popular requests were official skills for AI coding assistants and an official CLI for automating certain tasks. We have a new collection of official agent skills for developers to try out. We've also done some research on how different models perform with these skills and how energy efficient they are so you can make informed choices about which models you'd like to use for your projects.

The CLI we're offering right now is a prototype and may still have some rough edges. But if you're experimenting with AI automation, it's a good option for you to test out ways to connect AI agents to your Wagtail projects through the API. We haven't heard of anyone letting their OpenClaw agent run absolutely wild with their Wagtail content (yet), but this CLI gives you the option to do just that if you enjoy living dangerously. And if you’d to see what that looks like as a demo, here is an example of combining the API, CLI, and skills to do content operations with DeepSeek Harness and Mistral Large 4:

Enhance your SEO metadata with the new SEO checks

The checks section has a new feature to help you optimize your metadata and make it more SEO-friendly. The meta titles and descriptions will appear in the checks section along with a rating of the lengths for each of them. The ratings are informed by typical search engine display budgets and will help you make your meta data better for search engines and bots to collect. There is also an option for you to view and review other meta tags for your page directly in the Wagtail admin. And it’s also available on all live pages, within the userbar:

Thank you to Freedom of the Press Foundation who helped make this happen via a feature sponsorship!

Serve different page representations from the same URL

Wagtail now has the option for you to offer the same page in different formats so that your content can be accessed more easily by different technologies. You could add a JSON format that makes your content easier to use through APIs, or you could use Markdown to make your content more digestible by AI agents, with less page furniture to go through. This is a generic capability for all kinds of content negotiations, so you can add other content formats based on your own customization needs.

Having a good sitemap helps make your content easier to catalog and digest by search engine crawlers and other bots. Our improvements in this release will help you create a sitemap that includes translated pages and includes all of the pages from different locales when you're using internationalization. That can increase the discoverability of your multilingual content and make it more likely to turn up in search results.

Automate more with an improved API and agent-ready tools in Wagtail 8.1
See how Wagtail 8.1 can help you be ready for what's next
Meagen Voss

Wagtail community manager

Previous post
A Wagtail demo in your browser

We are living through a big shift in how online content is created and consumed. Change is both exciting and scary. It's leading many people to ask, "What's happening to the Internet?"

Answering that question and then creating an online future that works for most people is going to take a lot more people and organizing and effort than a single open source project can provide. The way we're doing our part is by committing to make a CMS that gives users options instead of mandates.

Wagtail 8.1 continues to build on some of the key goals in our product strategy to equip our users for a future in which more people are using AI tools to automate tasks, build their own software, and interact with online content. Our last big release introduced a new version of the Wagtail REST API. This release includes an updated version of that API along with other features and tools to provide you with the flexibility you need to adapt to new advances and challenges of the Internet.

Write and fetch more content with the updated API

The newest version of the API includes more writeable content types, all typed according to the site’s data model. You can retrieve more detailed schemas for StreamField blocks and other data through the API now, which will help you access and edit more of your Wagtail content. Here is an example, inspecting what blocks are available on a content page and their exact fields:

We improved the Markdown output as well so that you can add more styled text for links, line breaks, multi-paragraph quotes, and nested lists. We also corrected the ways certain references are handled through the API and optimized the OpenAPI schema so it will work better for larger projects.

We're continuing to call this API a preview as we build and add more features. If there is anything you think we should prioritize, we definitely want to hear your feedback.

Access workflows through the API

One of the bigger changes we've added to the API in this release is the ability to access Wagtail workflows through the API. Workflows are used to moderate and review content in Wagtail. Now you can submit pages or snippets for moderation, approve or reject moderation tasks, resume a workflow after changes were requested, cancel workflows, and read a workflow’s status and history through the API.

You can still do all these tasks through the Wagtail admin. But with the new API access, you have even more options to automate and track tasks related to your workflows. And like with all API features, this is all documented and typed to simplify integration into other systems:

Add more automation with official agent skills and the prototype CLI

When we surveyed our community about the sort of AI-related developer features you wanted to see for Wagtail, two popular requests were official skills for AI coding assistants and an official CLI for automating certain tasks. We have a new collection of official agent skills for developers to try out. We've also done some research on how different models perform with these skills and how energy efficient they are so you can make informed choices about which models you'd like to use for your projects.

The CLI we're offering right now is a prototype and may still have some rough edges. But if you're experimenting with AI automation, it's a good option for you to test out ways to connect AI agents to your Wagtail projects through the API. We haven't heard of anyone letting their OpenClaw agent run absolutely wild with their Wagtail content (yet), but this CLI gives you the option to do just that if you enjoy living dangerously. And if you’d to see what that looks like as a demo, here is an example of combining the API, CLI, and skills to do content operations with DeepSeek Harness and Mistral Large 4:

Enhance your SEO metadata with the new SEO checks

The checks section has a new feature to help you optimize your metadata and make it more SEO-friendly. The meta titles and descriptions will appear in the checks section along with a rating of the lengths for each of them. The ratings are informed by typical search engine display budgets and will help you make your meta data better for search engines and bots to collect. There is also an option for you to view and review other meta tags for your page directly in the Wagtail admin. And it’s also available on all live pages, within the userbar:

Thank you to Freedom of the Press Foundation who helped make this happen via a feature sponsorship!

Serve different page representations from the same URL

Wagtail now has the option for you to offer the same page in different formats so that your content can be accessed more easily by different technologies. You could add a JSON format that makes your content easier to use through APIs, or you could use Markdown to make your content more digestible by AI agents, with less page furniture to go through. For example, here is what a blog post would look like transformed to Markdown:

This is a generic capability for all kinds of content negotiations, so you can add other content formats based on your own customization needs.

Faster, better multilingual sitemaps

Having a good sitemap helps make your content easier to catalog and digest by search engine crawlers and other bots. Our improvements in this release will help you create a sitemap that includes translated pages and includes all of the pages from different locales when you're using internationalization. That can increase the discoverability of your multilingual content and make it more likely to turn up in search results.

Here’s an example of what this looks like in practice, with the correct alternate hreflang meta tags:

We also now document how to cache generated sitemaps, which will definitely help for large sites.

Getting ready for your upgrade

Most of the big changes happened in our last major release, but there are still a few things to be aware of as you upgrade. First of all, if you are using internationalization, be aware that all of your locales will be added to your sitemap. Second, we are no longer supporting Python 3.10, so please upgrade to a newer version if you haven't already (Python 3.15 is supported!). Third, be aware that we plan to deprecate the v2 API in our next major release (9.0). The v2 API is fully supported in this release with no changes, but deprecation warnings will start appearing in Wagtail 8.2.

There are a few other deprecated functions to watch out for. You can read all about them in our full release notes. Let us know what you think, and join us at Wagtail Space to discuss the new release!

Automate more with an improved API and agent-ready tools in Wagtail 8.1
See how Wagtail 8.1 can help you be ready for what's next
Meagen Voss

Wagtail community manager

Previous post
A Wagtail demo in your browser

We are living through a big shift in how online content is created and consumed. Change is both exciting and scary. It's leading many people to ask, "What's happening to the Internet?"

Answering that question and then creating an online future that works for most people is going to take a lot more people and organizing and effort than a single open source project can provide. The way we're doing our part is by committing to make a CMS that gives users options instead of mandates.

Wagtail 8.1 continues to build on some of the key goals in our product strategy to equip our users for a future in which more people are using AI tools to automate tasks, build their own software, and interact with online content. Our last big release introduced a new version of the Wagtail REST API. This release includes an updated version of that API along with other features and tools to provide you with the flexibility you need to adapt to new advances and challenges of the Internet.

Write and fetch more content with the updated API

The newest version of the API includes more writeable content types, all typed according to the site’s data model. You can retrieve more detailed schemas for StreamField blocks and other data through the API now, which will help you access and edit more of your Wagtail content. Here is an example, inspecting what blocks are available on a content page and their exact fields:

We improved the Markdown output as well so that you can add more styled text for links, line breaks, multi-paragraph quotes, and nested lists. We also corrected the ways certain references are handled through the API and optimized the OpenAPI schema so it will work better for larger projects.

We're continuing to call this API a preview as we build and add more features. If there is anything you think we should prioritize, we definitely want to hear your feedback.

Access workflows through the API

One of the bigger changes we've added to the API in this release is the ability to access Wagtail workflows through the API. Workflows are used to moderate and review content in Wagtail. Now you can submit pages or snippets for moderation, approve or reject moderation tasks, resume a workflow after changes were requested, cancel workflows, and read a workflow’s status and history through the API.

You can still do all these tasks through the Wagtail admin. But with the new API access, you have even more options to automate and track tasks related to your workflows. And like with all API features, this is all documented and typed to simplify integration into other systems:

Add more automation with official agent skills and the prototype CLI

When we surveyed our community about the sort of AI-related developer features you wanted to see for Wagtail, two popular requests were official skills for AI coding assistants and an official CLI for automating certain tasks. We have a new collection of official agent skills for developers to try out. We've also done some research on how different models perform with these skills and how energy efficient they are so you can make informed choices about which models you'd like to use for your projects.

The CLI we're offering right now is a prototype and may still have some rough edges. But if you're experimenting with AI automation, it's a good option for you to test out ways to connect AI agents to your Wagtail projects through the API. We haven't heard of anyone letting their OpenClaw agent run absolutely wild with their Wagtail content (yet), but this CLI gives you the option to do just that if you enjoy living dangerously. And if you’d to see what that looks like as a demo, here is an example of combining the API, CLI, and skills to do content operations with DeepSeek Harness and Mistral Large 4:

Enhance your SEO metadata with the new SEO checks

The checks section has a new feature to help you optimize your metadata and make it more SEO-friendly. The meta titles and descriptions will appear in the checks section along with a rating of the lengths for each of them. The ratings are informed by typical search engine display budgets and will help you make your meta data better for search engines and bots to collect. There is also an option for you to view and review other meta tags for your page directly in the Wagtail admin. And it’s also available on all live pages, within the userbar:

Thank you to Freedom of the Press Foundation who helped make this happen via a feature sponsorship!

Serve different page representations from the same URL

Wagtail now has the option for you to offer the same page in different formats so that your content can be accessed more easily by different technologies. You could add a JSON format that makes your content easier to use through APIs, or you could use Markdown to make your content more digestible by AI agents, with less page furniture to go through. For example, here is what a blog post would look like transformed to Markdown:

This is a generic capability for all kinds of content negotiations, so you can add other content formats based on your own customization needs.

Faster, better multilingual sitemaps

Having a good sitemap helps make your content easier to catalog and digest by search engine crawlers and other bots. Our improvements in this release will help you create a sitemap that includes translated pages and includes all of the pages from different locales when you're using internationalization. That can increase the discoverability of your multilingual content and make it more likely to turn up in search results.

Here’s an example of what this looks like in practice, with the correct alternate hreflang meta tags:

We also now document how to cache generated sitemaps, which will definitely help for large sites.

Getting ready for your upgrade

Most of the big changes happened in our last major release, but there are still a few things to be aware of as you upgrade. First of all, if you are using internationalization, be aware that all of your locales will be added to your sitemap. Second, we are no longer supporting Python 3.10, so please upgrade to a newer version if you haven't already (Python 3.15 is supported!). Third, be aware that we plan to deprecate the v2 API in our next major release (9.0). The v2 API is fully supported in this release with no changes, but deprecation warnings will start appearing in Wagtail 8.2.

There are a few other deprecated functions to watch out for. You can read all about them in our full release notes. Let us know what you think, and join us at Wagtail Space to discuss the new release!

Sustainability

Content management with green practices built in

Because of the impact software has on the world's carbon footprint, we're committed to reducing the climate impact of Wagtail CMS. Here's how we're supporting greener choices in our software and our community.

We're building features to support sustainability

We want to help people who use Wagtail make the greenest choices they can, especially when it comes to images. Here are a couple key features that will help people manage images more sustainably.

AVIF and WEBP Image Support

AVIF and WEBP are modern image formats that have been shown to achieve much smaller file sizes than JPEG or PNG without losing quality. With the option to switch to these formats, you can slim down your images and reduce the resources needed to power your website.

Special image tags

The Wagtail picture tag generates images in multiple formats or sizes in a single batch rather than multiple actions. Using this code helps you make your website greener while also helping you manage the images you need for different devices.

Dark mode

Dark mode isn't just an accessibility feature. For people who use OLED screens, which are often found in smartphones and tablets, dark mode makes the screen more efficient. So not only is dark mode good for your eyes, it's good for the planet too.

We're measuring Wagtail's impact

By our estimate in 2025, Wagtail websites account for 5173 tons of CO2e/year for 6431 sites with 12 tCO2e/year average emissions per site.

See how Wagtail measures up

We're pursuing sustainability standards

The standards we're using to assess Wagtail, include the UN Sustainable Development Goals ITU L.1420, L.1430, and the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard – Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) as well as its additional ICT Sector Guidance.

We're pursuing green collaborations

Our latest sustainability features were created through internships supported by Google Summer of Code and through a collaboration with the Green Web Foundation and Green Coding Berlin.

Check out our latest collabroation

We work for the benefit of the industry at large

In 2025, we collaborated on grid awareness concepts for websites with a consortium of CMS makers convened thanks to the Green Web Foundation

Check out our latest collaboration

We've added sustainability to our docs

The Wagtail documentation has a section on sustainability and resources for creating greener websites.

Read our sustainability docs

We're aiming to make all our projects sustainable

We're working on reducing the impact and carbon emissions of this website, Wagtail.org, docs.wagtail.org, and guide.wagtail.org.

We also intend to review environmental and equality considerations as part of organizing Wagtail Space and other community events.

Our sustainability roadmap

A greener future for Wagtail CMS

As part of our commitment to reducing emissions, we've mapped out some changes we're planning to pursue as well as some key opportunities for improvement

Explore the roadmap

Join our effort! Here are a few ways you can contribute

We’d love to get feedback on the sustainability of Wagtail. Get in touch with us in #sustainability on the Wagtail Slack if you are testing Wagtail and want to report your findings, or have a look at our backlog of issues and improvements.

Sponsor a green feature

If your values align with ours and you're eager to have more tools for reducing the carbon emissions of your content, let's talk!

Explore sponsorship

Give us feedback

Send us a message to let us know how well our sustainability efforts are supporting yours. We'd love to hear from you.

Get in touch

Join our community

If you want to contribute your skills towards making Wagtail more sustainable, a great first step is to join the #sustainability channel in our Slack community.

Join our Slack

Sustainability

Content management with green practices built in

Because of the impact software has on the world's carbon footprint, we're committed to reducing the climate impact of Wagtail CMS. Here's how we're supporting greener choices in our software and our community.

We're building features to support sustainability

We want to help people who use Wagtail make the greenest choices they can, especially when it comes to images. Here are a couple key features that will help people manage images more sustainably.

AVIF and WEBP Image Support

AVIF and WEBP are modern image formats that have been shown to achieve much smaller file sizes than JPEG or PNG without losing quality. With the option to switch to these formats, you can slim down your images and reduce the resources needed to power your website.

Special image tags

The Wagtail picture tag generates images in multiple formats or sizes in a single batch rather than multiple actions. Using this code helps you make your website greener while also helping you manage the images you need for different devices.

Dark mode

Dark mode isn't just an accessibility feature. For people who use OLED screens, which are often found in smartphones and tablets, dark mode makes the screen more efficient. So not only is dark mode good for your eyes, it's good for the planet too.

We're measuring Wagtail's impact

By our estimate in 2025, Wagtail websites account for 5173 tons of CO2e/year for 6431 sites with 12 tCO2e/year average emissions per site.

See how Wagtail measures up

We're pursuing sustainability standards

The standards we're using to assess Wagtail, include the UN Sustainable Development Goals ITU L.1420, L.1430, and the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard – Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) as well as its additional ICT Sector Guidance.

We're pursuing green collaborations

Our latest sustainability features were created through internships supported by Google Summer of Code and through a collaboration with the Green Web Foundation and Green Coding Berlin.

Check out our latest collabroation

We work for the benefit of the industry at large

In 2025, we collaborated on grid awareness concepts for websites with a consortium of CMS makers convened thanks to the Green Web Foundation

metadata.description: Our sustainability policy for Wagtail CMS and our approach to sustainability within the Wagtail CMS project.

text.value:
Wagtail Space 2026

18-20 November

Find out more
Skip to main content
Sustainability

Content management with green practices built in

Because of the impact software has on the world's carbon footprint, we're committed to reducing the climate impact of Wagtail CMS. Here's how we're supporting greener choices in our software and our community.

We're building features to support sustainability

We want to help people who use Wagtail make the greenest choices they can, especially when it comes to images. Here are a couple key features that will help people manage images more sustainably.

AVIF and WEBP Image Support

AVIF and WEBP are modern image formats that have been shown to achieve much smaller file sizes than JPEG or PNG without losing quality. With the option to switch to these formats, you can slim down your images and reduce the resources needed to power your website.

Special image tags

The Wagtail picture tag generates images in multiple formats or sizes in a single batch rather than multiple actions. Using this code helps you make your website greener while also helping you manage the images you need for different devices.

Dark mode

Dark mode isn't just an accessibility feature. For people who use OLED screens, which are often found in smartphones and tablets, dark mode makes the screen more efficient. So not only is dark mode good for your eyes, it's good for the planet too.

We're measuring Wagtail's impact

By our estimate in 2025, Wagtail websites account for 5173 tons of CO2e/year for 6431 sites with 12 tCO2e/year average emissions per site.

See how Wagtail measures up

We're pursuing sustainability standards

The standards we're using to assess Wagtail, include the UN Sustainable Development Goals ITU L.1420, L.1430, and the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard – Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) as well as its additional ICT Sector Guidance.

We're pursuing green collaborations

Our latest sustainability features were created through internships supported by Google Summer of Code and through a collaboration with the Green Web Foundation and Green Coding Berlin.

Check out our latest collabroation

We work for the benefit of the industry at large

In 2025, we collaborated on grid awareness concepts for websites with a consortium of CMS makers convened thanks to the Green Web Foundation

Check out our latest collaboration

We've added sustainability to our docs

The Wagtail documentation has a section on sustainability and resources for creating greener websites.

Read our sustainability docs

We're aiming to make all our projects sustainable

We're working on reducing the impact and carbon emissions of this website, Wagtail.org, docs.wagtail.org, and guide.wagtail.org.

We also intend to review environmental and equality considerations as part of organizing Wagtail Space and other community events.

Our sustainability roadmap

A greener future for Wagtail CMS

As part of our commitment to reducing emissions, we've mapped out some changes we're planning to pursue as well as some key opportunities for improvement

Explore the roadmap

Join our effort! Here are a few ways you can contribute

We’d love to get feedback on the sustainability of Wagtail. Get in touch with us in #sustainability on the Wagtail Slack if you are testing Wagtail and want to report your findings, or have a look at our backlog of issues and improvements.

Sponsor a green feature

If your values align with ours and you're eager to have more tools for reducing the carbon emissions of your content, let's talk!

Explore sponsorship

Give us feedback

Send us a message to let us know how well our sustainability efforts are supporting yours. We'd love to hear from you.

Get in touch

Join our community

If you want to contribute your skills towards making Wagtail more sustainable, a great first step is to join the #sustainability channel in our Slack community.

Join our Slack

Personal Information

Our website has e-mail links and a contact form. These features facilitate the capture of personal information such as your first name, last name, company, email address and job title. Use of information

We use aggregated server access data to track visitor use of the website and to compile statistical reports on website activity. These activities are completed with the goal of continually improving our website functionality and customer service.

Sustainability

Content management with green practices built in

Because of the impact software has on the world's carbon footprint, we're committed to reducing the climate impact of Wagtail CMS. Here's how we're supporting greener choices in our software and our community.

We're building features to support sustainability

We want to help people who use Wagtail make the greenest choices they can, especially when it comes to images. Here are a couple key features that will help people manage images more sustainably.

AVIF and WEBP Image Support

AVIF and WEBP are modern image formats that have been shown to achieve much smaller file sizes than JPEG or PNG without losing quality. With the option to switch to these formats, you can slim down your images and reduce the resources needed to power your website.

Special image tags

The Wagtail picture tag generates images in multiple formats or sizes in a single batch rather than multiple actions. Using this code helps you make your website greener while also helping you manage the images you need for different devices.

Dark mode

Dark mode isn't just an accessibility feature. For people who use OLED screens, which are often found in smartphones and tablets, dark mode makes the screen more efficient. So not only is dark mode good for your eyes, it's good for the planet too.

We're measuring Wagtail's impact

By our estimate in 2025, Wagtail websites account for 5173 tons of CO2e/year for 6431 sites with 12 tCO2e/year average emissions per site.

See how Wagtail measures up

We're pursuing sustainability standards

The standards we're using to assess Wagtail, include the UN Sustainable Development Goals ITU L.1420, L.1430, and the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard – Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) as well as its additional ICT Sector Guidance.

We're pursuing green collaborations

Our latest sustainability features were created through internships supported by Google Summer of Code and through a collaboration with the Green Web Foundation and Green Coding Berlin.

Check out our latest collabroation

We work for the benefit of the industry at large

In 2025, we collaborated on grid awareness concepts for websites with a consortium of CMS makers convened thanks to the Green Web Foundation

Check out our latest collaboration

We've added sustainability to our docs

The Wagtail documentation has a section on sustainability and resources for creating greener websites.

Read our sustainability docs

We're aiming to make all our projects sustainable

We're working on reducing the impact and carbon emissions of this website, Wagtail.org, docs.wagtail.org, and guide.wagtail.org.

We also intend to review environmental and equality considerations as part of organizing Wagtail Space and other community events.

Our sustainability roadmap

A greener future for Wagtail CMS

As part of our commitment to reducing emissions, we've mapped out some changes we're planning to pursue as well as some key opportunities for improvement

Explore the roadmap

Join our effort! Here are a few ways you can contribute

We’d love to get feedback on the sustainability of Wagtail. Get in touch with us in #sustainability on the Wagtail Slack if you are testing Wagtail and want to report your findings, or have a look at our backlog of issues and improvements.

Sponsor a green feature

If your values align with ours and you're eager to have more tools for reducing the carbon emissions of your content, let's talk!

Explore sponsorship

Give us feedback

Send us a message to let us know how well our sustainability efforts are supporting yours. We'd love to hear from you.

Get in touch

Join our community

If you want to contribute your skills towards making Wagtail more sustainable, a great first step is to join the #sustainability channel in our Slack community.

Join our Slack
